newsitem.title: USA: NYNEX asks $77.1 mln Mass. rate reduction.
newsitem.headline: NYNEX asks $77.1 mln Mass. rate reduction.

text.p: NYNEX Corp said Monday it filed for a $77.1 million reduction in overall rates and rebates for residence and business services in Massachusetts.
The company, in an annual price filing with state regulators, proposed to reduce rates by $65.1 million and provide a one-time rebate of $12 million, or $3.14 per residence and business line.
Of the proposed $65.1 million decrease, about half, or $32.1 million, offsets the increase in the public phone coin rate to 25 cents from 10 cents, NYNEX said.
Absent the payphone increase, the rate cuts amount to $33 million for 1997, in line with past years, a spokesman said. NYNEX refunded $29.6 million in 1996 and $38 million in 1995.

The company proposed the one-time rebate to offset the revenue increase from the coin rate for the period from April 1, when the coin rate increased, to August 15, when all the new proposed changes would take effect. The changes would bring the total rate reductions and rebates to $144.7 million.
NYNEX said it met its monthly service quality standards in the state for the recent 12-month period, the 20th straight month it met the standards introduced by regulators in 1995.
